page: Amazon Web Services r6g.xlarge is a memory-optimized server instance powered by custom AWS Graviton processors. It features an arm64 architecture utilizing the ARMv8 Neoverse-N1 CPU model running at 2.5 GHz. The configuration includes 4 dedicated physical cores and 4 vCPUs, meaning there is no hyperthreading. It is equipped with 32.0 GB of system memory, yielding a high memory-to-core ratio of 8.0 GB per core. There is no local storage bundled with this instance, and it does not feature any GPU accelerators. Network connectivity is rated at a baseline bandwidth of 1 Gbps, managed via the AWS Nitro hypervisor.

Benchmark evaluations indicate that the r6g.xlarge delivers average single-core CPU performance, with a stress-ng single-core score of 1519.59. However, multi-core performance is relatively weak, as shown by a stress-ng multi-core score of 6051.15 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 3156.0. Memory bandwidth tests show average performance for large blocks, reaching 70.15 GB/sec for read operations and 34.19 GB/sec for write operations, though small-block cached reads are weaker. Database operations on Passmark score in the average tier at 2654.31, while Redis SET operations achieve 4.73 million operations per second. Cryptographic operations benefit from hardware-accelerated AES support, though the CPU lacks AVX, AMX, and other vector extensions.

The instance represents a cost-efficient option for workloads requiring high memory density relative to compute power, leveraging the power-efficient ARM architecture. However, tradeoffs include poor performance in complex decompression tasks, such as bzip3, and low throughput for LLM inference. The lack of local storage requires reliance on network-attached storage. This server is best suited for memory-intensive workloads that do not demand extreme compute performance, such as caching layers, database operations, and general-purpose memory-bound applications.
